# gamlss2: Infrastructure for Flexible Distributional Regression

## Overview

The `gamlss2` package provides infrastructure for generalized additive models
for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS) and distributional regression more
generally. It reimplements the classic
[`gamlss`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=gamlss) framework with an emphasis
on estimation speed and flexible model components. Its modular design supports
alternative estimation algorithms, Bayesian sampling, and model terms such as
regression trees and forests.

Models can use smooth terms from
[`mgcv`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mgcv), custom special terms, and
response families with more than four parameters. Separate predictors for
the distribution parameters are specified in a single formula.

* The main model function is [`gamlss2()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/gamlss2.html).
* The default optimizer is [`RS()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/RS_CG.html); alternative optimizers can be supplied.
* The main methods are `summary()`, [`plot()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/plots.html), and [`predict()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/predict.gamlss2.html).
* Custom family objects are described in [Family Objects](families.html).
* Custom predictor components are described in [Special Model Terms](specials.html).

Start with [First Steps](firststeps.html) for a worked example, or browse the
manual pages.

```{r}
#| eval: false
help(package = "gamlss2")
```

## Installation

The development version of `gamlss2` can be installed via

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("gamlss2",
  repos = c("https://gamlss-dev.R-universe.dev",
            "https://cloud.R-project.org"))
```
